item.title: About
item.description: How to read this.

item.title: Aris
item.description:
Eri’s mentor and surrogate father. Knows the ancient texts and the properties of obsidian and the void. He makes the void vials and the dissolution tonic.

Beyond

He dies in the castle siege, spending his last void vial to seal Lachesis safe. The mob kills him. Eri feels his life-thread snap, and the grief triggers her breakthrough blink.

item.title: Burill
item.description:
Daughter of Mello, sixteen or seventeen, captain of the Everwind. Brash, teasing, light Doric accent. Eri’s closest friend from the sea years.

Beyond

She was laughing, and then she was dead – killed by a unicorn’s iridescent horn.

item.title: Eleutheria
item.description: Home of the pirates who took Eri in. She was dropped off around age seven and stayed one to two years.

item.title: Eri
item.description:
Fourteen at the story’s start. A defiant punk – outwardly confident, practical, observant, dry. Secretly the princess of Kraeta.

She refuses to stay blind.

Beyond

Daughter of King Lachesis and Queen Hren. Her father set an anchor on her forehead at age four; it is what unlocks the blink.

item.title: Heron
item.description:
An ancient dragon. The truth-teller.

Beyond

He reveals the real history: the unicorns built the obelisk, the rainbows drain life, the dragons were broken and now sustain Nephimhr with their own essence and are bound there. “In that moment of release, we found we could act.” He survives and reclaims the mountains.

item.title: Issah
item.description:
Mercenary. Deadpan, economical, a death-wish underneath. Travels east with Eri.

Beyond

His little brother Urmez starved to death in his arms. He earned the Dragon Slayer title through Malachar’s willing sacrifice. He kills Rhodes at the climax.

item.title: King Lachesis
item.description:
King of Kraeta. Eri’s father. Cold and distant on the surface; a fierce, hidden love underneath – a lock of her hair, birthday letters never sent.

Beyond

He holds the Golden Path and saw that Eri was the only thread that defeats the unicorns. He engineered everything to armour her against Rhodes’s paradise: the anchor, the hard life, the pirate years. He is trapped in a void bubble mid-book.

item.title: Kraeta
item.description: An island-continent kingdom. Eri’s home.

item.title: Malachar
item.description: A dragon. She let herself be killed so that Issah would become the Dragon Slayer and turn the prophecy.

item.title: Mello
item.description: Captain of the Pirates of Eleutheria. Weathered, fond, a father-figure. Took Eri in for the King’s seasoning and called her and Burill proper sailors.

item.title: Nephimhr
item.description:
The dragons’ refuge.

Beyond

They sustain it with their own essence, and are bound there by it.

item.title: Queen Hren
item.description:
Queen of Kraeta. Eri’s mother. Rhodes says she leapt from a cliff.

Beyond

Rhodes lies. She gave herself to his cause, and when her usefulness ran out he discarded her to the homunculi. Her arc mirrors Eri’s: both offered paradise, both forced to choose.

item.title: Rhodes
item.description:
A unicorn. Beautiful and terrible.

Beyond

The beauty is an illusion over a true rotting form. His weapon is paradise – temptation, never force; he holds that a soul coerced does not count. He deploys beasts as enforcers, lies to Eri about her mother, and cranks the drain to punish her. Issah kills him; the illusion collapses to rot.

item.title: The Anchor
item.description:
A mark set on Eri’s forehead by her father when she was four.

Beyond

It is what unlocks the blink.

item.title: The Blink
item.description:
Eri enters the thread dimension and transports to where a person once physically stood, found along their lifeline thread.

Location, not time. It has a cost.

Beyond

The cost is emotional hollowing. The still-point – going empty – is how she masters it, and it is what empties her.

item.title: The Drain
item.description:
Life pulled from the world through lenses, cast through the obelisk, and thrown back as rainbows.

Beyond

It is a dial. Boil the frog slowly, and crank it up to punish.

item.title: The Everwind
item.description: Burill’s ship.

item.title: The Golden Path
item.description: Lachesis’s foresight – the tapestry of time. He sees the threads.

item.title: The Green-Thumbs
item.description: A conspiratorial faction. Their agents stoke the mob against the King and plot long-term economic infiltration. Endurance always wins.

item.title: The Homunculi
item.description: The unicorns’ creatures and enforcers.

item.title: The Obelisk
item.description:
Obsidian. It stands on an outcrop near the summit, its tip exceeding the peak.

Beyond

It is a prism. The unicorns built it. Everything the lenses take passes through it and comes out as light.

item.title: The Obelisk
item.description: The whole shape of the book, one facet at a time.

item.title: The Still Point
item.description:
Control through release. To blink cleanly, let the feeling go.

Beyond

It is the tragic loop: releasing emotion to blink is exactly what hollows her. She saves the world and loses the ability to feel it.

item.title: The Thread Dimension
item.description: A tapestry of every life. Each thread is a person, and a thread can be followed to where that person once stood.

item.title: The Turning
item.description:
The story everyone is taught: the rainbows are the gods’ gift of peace.

Beyond

It is propaganda. The rainbows are the visible exhaust of the drain.

item.title: The Unicorns
item.description:
The parasites.

Beyond

They drain life through lenses into the obsidian obelisk, which prisms it into the rainbows. They rule by divide-and-conquer – they set the tribes and creatures against each other and directed the Vessel People to break the dragons – and by manufactured consent: controlled schooling and the Turning myth.

item.title: The Vessel People
item.description: A people the unicorns directed against the dragons.

item.title: Urmez
item.description: Issah’s little brother. He starved to death in Issah’s arms – Urmez around six, Issah around twelve.

item.title: Void Vials
item.description:
Aris’s work. Obsidian and the void, bottled.

Beyond

One of them seals Lachesis safe. It costs Aris his life.
